grounding:
TITLE: KIMI K2.5: VISUAL AGENTIC INTELLIGENCE  
AUTHORS: Kimi Team  
ONE-LINE TAKEAWAY: Kimi K2.5 achieves state-of-the-art results across coding, vision, reasoning, and agentic tasks with Agent Swarm reducing latency by up to 4.5× over single-agent baselines.  
- Sequential agent execution leads to linear scaling of inference time, causing high latency and limiting task complexity.  
- Existing multimodal models often suffer from modality conflict and poor cross-modal generalization.  
- Joint text-vision pre-training with early fusion at a constant low ratio (10%) throughout training.  
- Zero-vision SFT using only text data to activate visual reasoning and tool use.  
- Joint text-vision reinforcement learning (RL) that enhances both modalities simultaneously.  
- Agent Swarm framework enabling dynamic decomposition of complex tasks into parallel subtasks.  
- Parallel-Agent Reinforcement Learning (PARL) where only the orchestrator is updated during training.  
- Agent Swarm reduces inference latency by up to 4.5× compared to single-agent baselines.  
- Agent Swarm improves item-level F1 from 72.8% to 79.0% in wide-search scenarios.  
- Vision RL improves MMLU-Pro from 84.7% to 86.4%.  
- Vision RL improves GPQA-Diamond from 84.3% to 86.4%.  
- Vision RL improves LongBench v2 from 56.7% to 58.9%.  
- 4.5×: Latency reduction by Agent Swarm over single-agent baselines.  
- 79.0%: Item-level F1 improvement with Agent Swarm in wide-search scenarios.  
- 86.4%: MMLU-Pro accuracy after vision RL.  
- 86.4%: GPQA-Diamond accuracy after vision RL.  
- Figure 1: Main results of Kimi K2.5 across multiple domains.  
- Figure 2: Vision RL training curves showing performance improvement on vision benchmarks starting from zero-vision SFT.  
- Figure 3: Architecture of Agent Swarm with a trainable orchestrator creating specialized frozen subagents.  
- Figure 4: Performance progression showing cumulative reward increase as the orchestrator learns parallelization strategies.
